messages:
pagerbot: PD page fired PD-87291 — service=inference-dedicated, region=us-west-2. Trigger: 5xx spike on /v1/generate. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-87291 :rotating_light:

incidentbot: @here automated alert: 503 rate increased from 0.4% -> 18% over last 3m for dedicated pool 'dedicated-pool-usw2'. Suppression: none. Estimated customers affected: ~8. Suggested runbook: /runbooks/dedicated-pool-503

Alex G: I'm on it — grabbing bridge and initial triage. Claiming PD-87291 :raised_hand:

Sam T: seeing backend batcher OOMs in the logs, repeated "kvcache evict" around the same time. Correlation with a surge of long prompts from one customer id.

Alex G: quick question — is this customer-facing or internal test traffic?

Sam T: confirmed customer traffic (id: cust_9f2). Sample log: ```2026-03-15T20:14:02Z worker-7 ERROR batcher: OOM while building batch (size=1024)````

incidentbot: Runbook snippet: \n- Step 1: Enable burst capacity for dedicated pool (api: POST /pools/dedicated/scale?delta=+2)
- Step 2: Kick rolling restart for worker set (kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-worker)
- Step 3: If errors persist, reroute traffic to compatible model-variant (fallback policy)

Alex G: applied step1 (burst +2) and step2 (rolling restart). Monitoring.

Jin L: adding temporary client-side safety: set prompt timeout 2s and smaller chunking for suspected long prompts. Patch: ```service.config.client.timeout_ms = 2000```

Maria C: I'll take over in ~15m once Alex has baseline reduced. If it doesn't stabilize I'll take the bridge. @Alex ping me when you hand off. :eyes:

Alex G: status ping — error rate dropped from 18% -> 5% after scaling + restart. Latency stable. I'll hand off to Maria in 12m unless it resurges.

Sam T: found additional signal — kvcache eviction spike coincident with a parallel prefetch storm. Proposed immediate mitigation: limit prefetch parallelism to 8, rolling patch queued on canary. Patch snippet: ```prefetch.max_parallel = 8```

incidentbot: PD auto-escalation triggered at T+10m — escalated to Tier2. Audit: ack by Alex G at 1739999999 recorded.

Alex G: customer impact note: intermittent 503s for a small subset of requests and a handful of customers; no data loss, no customer data exposure. Drafting a short customer-facing note.

Maria C: drafting customer blurb now: "We're investigating intermittent 503s affecting a small subset of requests. Mitigations are in place and we see error rates markedly reduced. We'll follow up with a post-incident summary if degradation recurs." Will push to SRE-comm.

Sam T: canary patch applied to prefetch limiter, monitoring metrics. Early look: error rate on canary host dropped to <1%.

Alex G: handoff now — handing ownership to Maria C at 1740000300. Leaving a quick checklist: \n- burst scaling active\n- rolling restart in progress (complete on 3/5 nodes)\n- prefetch limiter patched on canary\n- client timeout temp set

Maria C: ack taking owner. I'll continue monitoring and create follow-up ticket (SRE-2026-042) plus timeline notes. Planning 1hr follow-up to decide postmortem. :thumbsup:

incidentbot: PD note appended: owner changed to Maria C at 1740000300.

Alex G: last quick check before leaving — error rate steady <1% for the last 3m, no new customers reporting. Good handoff.

Maria C: thanks, everyone. I'll mark resolved once we're confident and will publish the customer note if steady for 30m. Will schedule a postmortem if we see recurrence. :spiral_calendar:

pagerbot: PD-87291 status update: resolved (owner=Maria C) at 1740000600.
